title: Rigveda 6.74: To Soma and Rudra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.74: To Soma and Rudra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.74 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Soma and Rudra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 489v-490r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.74.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 490r
translation.original_text:
1somā̍rudrā dhā̱raye̍thām asu̱rya1̱̍m pra vā̍m i̱ṣṭayo 'ra̍m aśnuvantu | dame̍-dame sa̱pta ratnā̱ dadhā̍nā̱ śaṁ no̍ bhūtaṁ dvi̱pade̱ śaṁ catu̍ṣpade ||
2somā̍rudrā̱ vi vṛ̍hata̱ṁ viṣū̍cī̱m amī̍vā̱ yā no̱ gaya̍m āvi̱veśa̍ | ā̱re bā̍dhethā̱ṁ nirṛ̍tim parā̱cair a̱sme bha̱drā sau̍śrava̱sāni̍ santu ||
3somā̍rudrā yu̱vam e̱tāny a̱sme viśvā̍ ta̱nūṣu̍ bheṣa̱jāni̍ dhattam | ava̍ syatam mu̱ñcata̱ṁ yan no̱ asti̍ ta̱nūṣu̍ ba̱ddhaṁ kṛ̱tam eno̍ a̱smat ||
4ti̱gmāyu̍dhau ti̱gmahe̍tī su̱śevau̱ somā̍rudrāv i̱ha su mṛ̍ḻataṁ naḥ | pra no̍ muñcata̱ṁ varu̍ṇasya̱ pāśā̍d gopā̱yata̍ṁ naḥ sumana̱syamā̍nā ||
translation.text:
1HOLD fast your Godlike sway, O Soma-Rudra: let these our sacrifices quickly reach you. Placing in every house your seven great treasures, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.
2Soma and Rudra, chase to every quarter the sickness that hath visited our dwelling. Drive Nirr̥iti away into the distance, and give us excellent and happy glories.
3Provide, O Soma-Rudra, for our bodies all needful medicines to heal and cure us. Set free and draw away the sin committed which we have still inherent in our persons.
4Armed with keen shafts and weapons, kind and loving, be gracious unto us, Soma and Rudra. Release us from the noose of Varuṇa; keep us from sorrow, in your tender loving-kindness.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 490r (numbered 11r by the scribe) (OPenn image 490, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.74.1 ‹sapta ratnā dadhānā śam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 490v (numbered 11v by the scribe), begins in RV 6.75.3 ‹vakṣyantī-iva it ā ganīganti›. Verses 6.74.1-4 end on this page; 6.74.1 begins on fol. 489v (numbered 10v by the scribe).
